# Proofs are generated by a prover the player controls

Midnight's prover sees the witnesses, which in this game include a player's deck key and cards. Every player therefore proves on a machine they control. The prototype prover is Midnight's own prover compiled to wasm and run inside the player's browser (`midnight-zkir-wasm`, built from source by `scripts/build-prover.sh`): no separate process, nothing to install, witnesses never leave the page. No prover operated by us receives a player's witnesses, ever. Proving sits behind the ledger's `ProvingProvider` interface so that other user-controlled provers -- a native one for desktop players, the proof server in Docker, whatever the wallet may offer -- replace the wasm one without touching the game. The onboarding requirement is fixed only after the wallet, prover and headset browser have been tested together.

## Considered options

- A prover hosted by us: convenient for players, but it would see every card, which is the thing the whole design exists to prevent.
- The proof server in Docker on each player's machine: honest, but an install step, and unavailable in a headset. Kept as an alternative prover behind the same interface.

## Consequences

- Proving time is the browser's single-threaded wasm time until the prover is built with threads: about 2 minutes for the shuffle circuit at k=17 on a laptop (`docs/protocol/dealing.md`, results). Shrinking that is the next piece of work on the protocol.
- 2026-09-16: Midnight's DApp connector API 4.x lets a wallet lend its prover (`getProvingProvider`, the ledger's `ProvingProvider` shape). The wallet is the player's own software, so this is a fourth user-controlled prover behind the same interface, and the one a headset player is most likely to have. Not tried yet.
- Measured 2026-09-15 (`docs/protocol/dealing.md`, results): threads gain little in wasm (the prover's interpretation phase is single-threaded), the k=16 shuffle proves in 77 s in wasm and 4.4 s natively on the same machine. So the wasm prover is the zero-install default and the only headset option, desktop players get a native prover behind the same interface (`prover/native` grown into a local helper, the Docker proof server, or a wallet's), and the deck of a deal is ready when the slowest prover at the table has shuffled; deadlines follow the prover a player declares.
